reviewerRole: B25 LLM Vision UX Judge Agent
reviewMethod: Fresh screenshot-first review using supplied artifacts, Product Docs V2 community experience docs, production UX blueprint, screen matrix, workflow/persona matrix, visual inspection audit, and current screenshot pixels only.
inputsReviewed: current screenshot files referenced in independent-production-ux-review.json

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Does the whole experience feel like a real production community app for the target users, not merely an implemented workflow harness?
holisticQuestionAnswers.why: The screenshots show a repeated workflow-card renderer across unrelated communities and several rows still read as review/status evidence rather than real production product surfaces.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Replace repeated workflow cards with distinct domain-native surfaces and recapture the affected workflows.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Is the UI modern, easy to use, easy to navigate, and visually appealing for the target persona?
holisticQuestionAnswers.why: The UI is readable and uses icons, but the dominant experience is oversized stacked cards, dense explanatory copy, one-note palettes, and repeated layout structure that makes navigation and task differentiation weak.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Introduce surface-specific product layouts and reduce dense status-card repetition.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Is the overall information architecture organized around community content and real jobs-to-be-done instead of workflow lists or validation surfaces?
holisticQuestionAnswers.why: The screenshots contain domain labels such as events, donations, care, ballots, and exports, but the IA is still mostly a vertical list of task cards rather than feeds, inboxes, dashboards, detail pages, forms, and histories that match each community job.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Rebuild top-level community IA and workflow entry states around real content sections and job-specific surfaces.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Does the copy sound like product language rather than workflow/spec/test language?
holisticQuestionAnswers.why: Visible copy repeatedly uses phrases like review the details, final review, wizard progress, checkout review, local package details, and preview the community experience for each member role.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Rewrite copy as user-facing product language and hide diagnostics/harness text.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Are title truncation, clipping, crowding, repeated-card fatigue, over-prominent platform banners, one-note palettes, and default-scaffold cues absent?
holisticQuestionAnswers.why: Long app-bar titles truncate, lower content is clipped below the viewport on many cards, community palettes are largely one hue, and the same card shell repeats across nearly all evidence rows.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Fix responsive title treatment, reduce oversized cards, vary component structure, and recapture evidence.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Does the screen set provide concrete content and lifecycle actions a real user needs?
holisticQuestionAnswers.why: Nine workflow/persona scorecards and twenty-two lifecycle scorecards remain failing in the supplied evidence, and screenshot review confirms member receiver, payment, ad-off, export, and social/ad states are still incomplete or generic.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Complete domain lifecycle states and prove them with fresh screenshots.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Can B25 pass from the visible screenshots reviewed in this run?
holisticQuestionAnswers.why: There are unresolved major screenshot-backed findings. B25 cannot pass until blocker and major findings are zero.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Remediate major findings, rebuild, recapture, and rerun the B25 evidence and judge sequence.

findings.title: Primary experiences still use one repeated workflow-card renderer across unrelated communities
findings.summary: The screenshots show the same one-column stack of large rounded cards, icon circles, pill chips, review/status panels, and a single bottom action repeated across Garden Club, Book Club, Soccer, HOA, Masjid Nur, Chess, Camera, Platform Social, Ad-Free, and Export/Migration surfaces. The labels are more domain-specific, but the product still reads as a workflow-card template rather than distinct event, payment, inbox, request, export, receipt, and admin-review products.
visibleEvidence: Garden Club row b25-v4-row-001 shows a hero card plus stacked Care/Plant/Export cards rather than a richer club hub.
Book Club row b25-v4-row-010 uses the same large card, pill checklist, review box, and submit button for a nomination.
Chess Club row b25-v4-row-100 uses the same shell for a club home and match result.
Data Portability row b25-v4-row-130 uses the same card shell for an import wizard instead of a dense transfer dashboard.
Ad-Free row b25-v4-row-124 uses the same review/status card pattern for checkout instead of a payment checkout surface.
findings.requiredFix: Replace the repeated card renderer with domain-native product surfaces per community: event detail/RSVP, feed/inbox/thread, donation/payment checkout, receipt/history, protected care request form, admin review queue, social connection guard, export/import wizard, and transfer status screens with visibly distinct layouts and content density.

findings.title: Visible copy still exposes review/spec/harness framing instead of natural product language
findings.summary: Many screenshots use copy such as "Review the details", "Final review", "Wizard progress", "Checkout review", "Local package details", and "Preview the community experience for each member role". This text describes the validation model or internal review state rather than what a real member, owner, donor, guardian, or admin would naturally see.

Data Portability row b25-v4-row-130 labels the flow "Wizard progress".
Persona picker row b25-v4-row-186 says "Preview the community experience for each member role."

findings.requiredFix: Rewrite user-facing copy as domain product language. Remove review/spec/test phrasing and local package or persona-preview copy from production-facing screens. Put implementation metadata behind diagnostics, not in the primary community experience.

findings.title: Distinct screen rows reuse identical screenshot hashes and do not prove distinct production states
findings.summary: The evidence contains 195 screen rows but only 181 unique screenshot hashes. Several distinct workflows or persona states share identical pixels, so the screenshots do not prove separate user-facing states for those rows.
visibleEvidence: Masjid announcement start/action/result screenshots are reused by wf-community-persona-aware-ux and wf-multi-persona-workflow-evidence rows.
Export import replay rows b25-v4-row-130 through b25-v4-row-132 share hashes with export import preview rows b25-v4-row-175 through b25-v4-row-177.
Full export bundle rows b25-v4-row-133 through b25-v4-row-135 share hashes with redacted bundle rows b25-v4-row-157 through b25-v4-row-159.
Persona role inventory dialog row b25-v4-row-185 and demo persona picker row b25-v4-row-186 share the same screenshot hash.
findings.requiredFix: Recapture or redesign the affected workflows so every distinct workflow/persona/state has visibly distinct content, state, and lifecycle proof. If two rows intentionally share a surface, merge the evidence rather than claiming separate production states.

findings.title: Workflow lifecycles are not visually complete enough for production handoff, receipt, and recovery states
findings.summary: The screenshots still leave major workflow/persona lifecycle gaps. Some flows show a review/status card without the required domain decision, alternate/change path, durable receipt/history, receiver state, or continuation state. The member-side Masjid announcement still looks like an announcement composer; payment and ad-off flows show review/status summaries rather than full checkout/receipt/management surfaces; export flows miss distinct preview/redaction/checksum/rollback proof.
visibleEvidence: Masjid member receiver row b25-v4-row-193 shows "Announcement composer" and "before publishing" copy while the member is supposed to receive/read the announcement.
Masjid donation rows b25-v4-row-052 through b25-v4-row-054 show "Sadaqah donation receipt" and repeated checkout-review panels rather than a complete payment and receipt lifecycle.
Ad-Free checkout rows b25-v4-row-124 through b25-v4-row-126 list payer/payment/entitlement concepts but do not show a production checkout with payment method, receipt ID, or management history.

Export rows b25-v4-row-130 through b25-v4-row-183 repeatedly show generic wizard progress/status cards and duplicate screenshots instead of distinct preview, redaction, checksum, retry, and rollback states.
findings.requiredFix: For each affected workflow/persona pair, capture entry, decision, primary action, alternate/change/reject path, persistent result, receipt/history/status, and receiver/continuation states in visible UI. The member/receiver state must not reuse actor/composer copy.

findings.title: Visual polish remains below the production bar because of title truncation, dense card stacks, and one-note palettes
findings.summary: The screenshots are readable but not yet shippable as a modern production app. Long community names truncate in the app bar, many screens are dominated by one hue per community, and large dense cards push critical content below the fold. The repeated card layout makes unrelated tasks feel like the same screen with swapped text.
visibleEvidence: App bars visibly truncate long names such as Neighborhood Book Club, Riverside Youth Soccer, Cedar Commons HOA, and Data Portability Community.
Most communities use a single dominant color family across background, cards, chips, and buttons.
Rows such as b25-v4-row-001, b25-v4-row-010, b25-v4-row-100, b25-v4-row-124, and b25-v4-row-130 show critical content only as stacked text cards, with lower content clipped below the viewport.
findings.requiredFix: Improve production visual hierarchy: shorter responsive app-bar titles or branded headers, more varied domain components, less oversized card stacking, clearer section density, and layouts that make primary decisions visible without excessive scroll.
